Agromet Advisory Bulletin for the Coimbatore District 
Bulletin No.073/2026 Issued on 11.09.2026 
(From 12th September 2026 to 16th September 2026) 
Issued jointly by Agro Climate Research Centre, TNAU 
 
 
Past Weather for Tamil Nadu  
Weather Summary for the period since the issue of last bulletin 072 (08.09.2026) for Tamil Nadu. 
Maximum temperature ranged from 33°C to 41°C and minimum temperature ranged from 2 2°C to 30°C, 
over the State. Kodaikanal and Udhagamandalam recorded m aximum temperature ranged from 20 oC to 
22oC and minimum temperature ranged from 09oC to14°C. 
 
Coimbatore District Past Weather  
In Coimbatore district , during 08.09.2026 to 10 .09.2026 the max imum temperature was recorded 
34°C and minimum temperature was 22-23°C. The morning r elative humidity recorded was 71 -75% and 
evening relative humidity was 52-57%. The average wind speed recorded was 30-32 km per hour and the 
wind directions were from South West direction.

Weather forecast for next five days:  (12.09.2026 to 16.09.2026) 
According to district forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department for C oimbatore 
district, sky will be mostly cloudy. Light to Moderate rainfall is expected in Western Ghats regions of 
some places and Light rainfall is expected in other parts of Coimbatore . Maximum tempera ture is 
expected to be around 31-34°C. Minimum tempe rature is expected to be around 20-23°C. Morning 
relative humidity is expected to be around 80-90% and evening relative humidity is expected  to be 
between 50-60%. Average wind speed is expected to be around 10-12 km per hour and the wind 
directions will be from South West direction.

Weather Warning  
12.09.2026 to 15.09.2026 : Thunderstorms & Lightning, Squall etc. 
16.09.2026 : No Warning 
 
Weather Warning on Agriculture 
Thunderstorms & lightning, squally wind is expected in some places and hence farmers are requested to 
stake banana crop which are more than five month old.  
 
Agro Advisory 
 
Crop Stage Advisory 
General  Drizzling or Light rainfall is expected in the western zone  for the 
forth coming wee k. 15th & 16 th September may get 15 -20mm of 
rainfall in all three districts. 
Isolated places along the Western Ghats may receive thunderstorm. 
Hence, avoid trespassing and animal grazing near Western Ghats. 
Irrigation may be  continued based on the soil moisture. Provide 
adequate draining to young crops. 
Rice Nursery  
Sowing 
Due to prevailing weather, Thrips insect attack is observed in Samba 
paddy nursery. Spray Azadirachtin 0.15% @ 2ml per lit of water. 
Also watch for diseases. 
In the absence of wet nursery and if sufficient ground water is 
available, direct dry seeding of medi um duration rice can be done 
with the anticipated rain for Samba season. 
Sorghum, 
Cumbu 
Land preparation By utilizing the anticipated rainfall, land preparation may be initiated 
in rainfed black soil towards pre monsoon sowing. 
Groundnut Land preparation With the receipt of anticipated rainfall dry lands may be prepared for 
sowing groundnut and millets during North East Monsoon.   
Sugarcane Vegetative Prevailing wind speed is more than 10 km per hour along with light 
rainfall. Hence, five months old sugarcane may be propped against 
lodging.  
Tomato Vegetative Prevailing weather is favourable for sucking pests and leaf minor in 
tomato. Spray 3% neem Seed Kernel Extract to control the pests. 
Banana 5 months old Prevailing wind speed is more than 10 km per hour  along with light 
rainfall. Hence, five months old banana may be propped against 
lodging.

Turmeric Bulking Turmeric is at bulking stage, which is critical for both moisture stress 
and excess water. Hence, care to keep sufficient moisture and avoid 
excess moisture or over dry. 
Prevailing high relative humidity and wind speed would spread the 
spores of turmeric leaf spot from endemic area. Spray Mancozeb @ 1 
kg/ha or copper oxy chloride @ 1.25 kg/ha. 
Animals  Present high wind speed and relative humidity may forc e the animals 
to take more drinking water. Provide enough clean drinking water to 
the animals. 
Due to the prevailing wind speed, feeds of the poultry chicken gets 
wasted to avoid plant based oils may be mixed feeds of the poultry.  
 
SMS advisory: 
 With the receipt of anticipated rainfall dry lands may be prepared for sowing millets and pulses 
during North East Monsoon.    
 
 
 
 
 
Professor and Head 
Principal Nodal Officer (GKMS) 
Agro Climate Research Centre
